```text
422 {'error': 'error.unsupported_file'}
```

The three blocks of this page, with their imports in one place, are `examples/web_service.py`. `ThreadingHTTPServer`
gives each request its own thread, and all of them wait on the one reading thread.

## Before production

This is the shape, not a finished service. A real one also limits the size of an upload and the length of the queue,
answers before the read is done when a read may take minutes, and chooses the memory settings for its machine: each read
starts up to two workers, each budgeted 1,500 MB, and `Options(processes=1, backend="onnxruntime")` suits a small machine.
`result(timeout=300)` raises `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` when a read takes longer, and nothing here catches it:
decide what the caller is told, and whether the read should be cancelled ([Progress and cancel](progress-and-cancel.md)).

# docs/how-to/ai-assistants.md

# Use Extract from an AI coding assistant

An assistant that writes code against Extract from memory gets a few things wrong, always the same few, and some of them
fail silently. This page is for the person who reads what the assistant wrote; the rules for the assistant itself are in
`AGENTS.md`, at the root of the repository.

## Give the assistant the right files

- `AGENTS.md` is written for a coding assistant that has nothing else: runnable recipes for the common tasks, the fields
  it will use, and what never to do. Many coding assistants look for it on their own when they work inside the
  repository; if yours does not, name it in your request. For a project that only installs Extract, copy it into that
  project.
- `llms.txt` is an index of the documentation, with one line for each page.
- `llms-full.txt` is every page of this site as one plain file. Attach it when the assistant cannot browse the
  repository.

## The mistakes, and how they show

| What the assistant wrote | What you see | Why, and the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Reads at the top level of the script, with no `__main__` guard | A scan raises `EngineLoadError` after a few seconds (`cause="no_main_guard"`) and the script exits with status 1 | The workers import the script again. Put every call to `extract.read` and `extract.Reader` under `if __name__ == "__main__":` ([Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md#engineloaderror-the-script-reads-at-its-top-level)). |
| Calls `extract.read` for each file in a loop | Every file waits several seconds before its first page | `read` starts the workers and loads the models on every call. One [`Reader`](../reference/reader.md#reader) does it once. |
| Treats `ok` as checked, `unscored` as fine, or a returned document as read | Wrong words in the output that nobody was asked about | `ok` means the guard did not flag the word; `unscored` means nobody could judge it; a document with an unreadable page comes back `partial`, not raised. |
| Tests `word.status == "doubtful"` to ask whether a word is still open | Decided words come back | A decision sets `review` and leaves `status` alone: test `word.review is None`. |
| Calls `accept` or `use_suggestion` on every doubtful word, or `correct` with a guessed text | A clean document that nobody reviewed | A decision belongs to a person who has seen `Document.word_crop`. `use_suggestion` applies whatever is offered, even a digit change whose `verified` is false. |
| Asks a language model to fix a digit, or edits a number itself | A total that is right on screen and wrong in the books | Extract changes a digit only when a verifying rule confirms the new one, or when a person types it. |
| Uses `accept` to turn a `mismatch` into `checked` | The number stays `mismatch` | Only a rule makes a number `checked`. |
| Calls `use_suggestion` on an IBAN written in groups | `ValueError: ... has no suggestion` | The method handles a number made of one word, and a tie gives no suggestion. Use `Document.correct` on the word that holds the wrong digit. |
| Expects corrected words after a plain `read`, or sets `second_reading=True` for better text | Nothing changes, or a slower read that changes nothing | `correct` is `off` unless you ask for `safe` or `more`. `second_reading=True` computes readings that the packaged guard ignores: use `"thorough"` after fetching its models. |
| Saves with `Document.save` over a file it should keep | The old file is gone | `save` overwrites without asking; `export` never overwrites. |
| Exports `"pdf"` from a loaded reading | `SourceChanged` | The searchable PDF needs the source PDF with the same hash. Pass `source=` to `load`. |
| Reads in tests and examples with the default work folder | Files in the user's cache folder, and a cancel test that runs instantly the second time | Pass `Options(work_dir=<a temporary folder>)`: pages read before come from the cache with no OCR. |
| Starts two reads at once, or shares one `Reader` between threads | `ram.low` notices and a read that waits for memory | A read starts up to two workers of about 1.5 GB each. On 3 to 4 GB, use `Options(processes=1, backend="onnxruntime")` and one read at a time. |
| Writes `from extract import *`, imports `extract.engine`, or calls `doc.text` | `Warning` stops being the built-in, or an `AttributeError` | Write `import extract`. Only the 36 names of `extract.__all__` are public, and there is no `Document.text`: export `"txt"` instead. |
| Passes a JPEG, a Word file or a French document | `UnsupportedFile`, or many `doubtful` words | PDF only, Spanish and English only. Put images in a PDF first. |
| Expects invoice fields from a page after the first | `doc.invoice` is `None` or lacks fields | Fields are read from page 1 only, and a field that was not found is `None`. Test each one. |

## Check the code you were given

- Every call to `extract.read` or `extract.Reader` is under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
- Several files go through one `Reader`, in one thread.
- The code looks at `doc.status`, and at `doc.unreadable_pages` when it is `partial`.
- Nothing decides a doubtful word, or changes a number, without a person or a rule you can name.
- `Options(work_dir=...)` is set in tests and examples.
- `export` is used where a file must not be lost, and `save` only where overwriting is meant.
- Every name used is on the [reference index](../reference/index.md). If it is not there, it does not exist.

## A request that works

```text
Read AGENTS.md first. Write a script that reads every PDF in ./incoming with one extract.Reader and
Options(work_dir="work"), prints each document's status, writes a workbook for each into ./out, and lists the
words that need a decision with the page number. Do not accept or correct any word.
```

# docs/reference/index.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# API reference

Offline OCR for PDFs that says which words and numbers are probably wrong.

Extract reads a scanned or digital PDF on your own machine, with no network. It gives every word a status, checks the
numbers with the rules a number has to obey (check letters, sums, VAT), and exports a searchable PDF, a workbook, a JSON
file and a text file. Import the package as `import extract` and use the names below. Nothing else is public, apart
from three helpers for word ids in `extract.types` ([`word_id`](data-types.md#word_id), [`base_id`](data-types.md#base_id), [`page_of`](data-types.md#page_of)).

The names, by group:

- Reading: [`read`](functions.md#read), [`Reader`](reader.md#reader), [`load`](functions.md#load), [`inspect`](functions.md#inspect), [`Options`](options.md#options), [`CancelToken`](functions.md#canceltoken), [`FileInfo`](functions.md#fileinfo).
- The document: [`Document`](document.md#document), with its parts [`Page`](data-types.md#page-pagereading) (`PageReading`), [`Word`](data-types.md#word), [`Reason`](data-types.md#reason), [`Fix`](data-types.md#fix), [`Reading`](data-types.md#reading), [`Number`](data-types.md#number-numberresult)
  (`NumberResult`), [`Rule`](data-types.md#rule-ruleresult) (`RuleResult`), [`DigitSuggestion`](data-types.md#digitsuggestion), [`Invoice`](data-types.md#invoice-invoicefields) (`InvoiceFields`), [`InvoiceLine`](data-types.md#invoiceline), [`VatPair`](data-types.md#vatpair)
  and [`Cell`](data-types.md#cell).
- Events, for the `on_event` callback: [`Event`](events.md#event), [`Started`](events.md#started), [`PageRead`](events.md#pageread), [`Progress`](events.md#progress), [`DocumentRead`](events.md#documentread), [`Exported`](events.md#exported), [`Warning`](events.md#warning)
  and [`Finished`](events.md#finished).
- Errors: [`ExtractError`](errors.md#extracterror) and its subclasses [`UnsupportedFile`](errors.md#unsupportedfile), [`PasswordProtected`](errors.md#passwordprotected), [`EngineLoadError`](errors.md#engineloaderror),
  [`ModelMismatch`](errors.md#modelmismatch), [`OutputExists`](errors.md#outputexists), [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged) and [`Cancelled`](errors.md#cancelled).

Four names are shorter than the classes they stand for: `Page` is `PageReading`, `Number` is `NumberResult`, `Rule` is
`RuleResult` and `Invoice` is `InvoiceFields`; `repr` and `__name__` show the long name. `extract.Warning` is an event
class, not the built-in `Warning`: write `import extract` and use `extract.Warning`, never `from extract import *`,
which rebinds `Warning` in your module.

The names are imported on first use, so that importing a light submodule does not load the PDF, image and spreadsheet
libraries. The package is typed (`py.typed`), and `extract.__version__` is its version. Any script that reads a PDF
must put its calls under `if __name__ == "__main__":`, because the OCR runs in worker processes that import the script
again; see `read`.

**Example**

```python
import extract

print(extract.__version__)
print(extract.Page.__name__, extract.Number.__name__, extract.Rule.__name__, extract.Invoice.__name__)
print(len(extract.__all__))
```

```text
# output
5.0.7
PageReading NumberResult RuleResult InvoiceFields
36
```

`extract.__all__` has 36 names, each linked above to its entry. The fields of a saved reading are on [JSON format](json-format.md), the screens and keys of the interface on [Interface](interface.md), and the commands and scripts on [Command line](command-line.md).

## The samples the examples use

The examples read three invented sample documents. `scan.pdf`, `invoice.pdf` and `damaged.pdf` are copies of `tests/fixtures/doubtful.pdf`, `mismatch.pdf` and `unreadable.pdf`, and `scans/` holds the three. `scan.extract.json`, `invoice.extract.json` and `damaged.extract.json` are the saved readings of each, made by reading it once with the default `Options`. Run this once, from the root of the repository, to make them:

```python
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

import extract

SAMPLES = {"doubtful": "scan", "mismatch": "invoice", "unreadable": "damaged"}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    Path("scans").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with extract.Reader(extract.Options(work_dir="work")) as reader:
        for fixture, name in SAMPLES.items():
            shutil.copy(f"tests/fixtures/{fixture}.pdf", f"{name}.pdf")
            shutil.copy(f"{name}.pdf", f"scans/{name}.pdf")
            reader.read(f"{name}.pdf").save(f"{name}.extract.json")
```

Every name, address and number in the samples is invented. The examples use a `work` folder for the work folder (`Options.work_dir`), so that nothing is written into your own cache folder.

# docs/reference/functions.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# Functions and helpers

The three functions that start every program, `read`, `load` and `inspect`, and the two small classes that go with them: `FileInfo`, which `inspect` returns, and `CancelToken`, which stops a read from another thread.

## `read`

```text
read(
    path: str | Path,
    options: Options | None = None,
    on_event: Callable[[Event], None] | None = None,
    cancel: CancelToken | None = None,
    *,
    correct: str | None = None,
) -> Document
```

Read one PDF and return a [`Document`](document.md#document).

It starts the OCR worker processes and loads the models for this call, reads, and stops them again: several
seconds before the first page, paid on every call. To read two files or more, make one [`Reader`](reader.md#reader) and call
[`Reader.read`](reader.md#readerread) for each.

Digital PDFs whose text layer reads as text need no OCR, and scanned pages that were read before come from the
page cache in the work folder, keyed by the file's hash, the page, the resolution and the engine.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| Path` | required | The PDF, as a string or a `Path`. |
| `options` | `Options \| None` | `None` | The [`Options`](options.md#options) of the read. `None` means `Options()`, whose work folder is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/extract`, or `~/.cache/extract`; pass `Options(work_dir=...)` in tests, and wherever the page cache and the logs must go elsewhere. |
| `on_event` | `Callable[[Event], None] \| None` | `None` | A function called with each [`Event`](events.md#event) of the read ([`Started`](events.md#started), [`PageRead`](events.md#pageread), [`Progress`](events.md#progress), [`DocumentRead`](events.md#documentread), [`Warning`](events.md#warning), [`Finished`](events.md#finished)). It runs in the thread that called `read`. |
| `cancel` | `CancelToken \| None` | `None` | A [`CancelToken`](#canceltoken) that stops the read from another thread or from `on_event`. |
| `correct` | `str \| None` | `None` | `off`, `safe` or `more`, overriding `Options.correct` for this read. `None` uses the option. It is the only option `read` takes directly: `languages`, `review`, `second_reading` and the others go in `Options`. Keyword-only. |

**Returns**

The `Document`. Check [`Document.status`](document.md#documentstatus): a document with an unreadable page comes back `partial`, it is not an error.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: `correct` is not `off`, `safe` or `more`.
- `FileNotFoundError`: `path` does not exist. This is the built-in exception, not an [`ExtractError`](errors.md#extracterror).
- [`UnsupportedFile`](errors.md#unsupportedfile): The file is not a PDF that can be opened.
- [`PasswordProtected`](errors.md#passwordprotected): The PDF needs a password to be opened.
- [`EngineLoadError`](errors.md#engineloaderror): A piece the read needs is missing or cannot start: the word lists, the guard model, an OCR model, or a worker process. The message says which.
- [`ModelMismatch`](errors.md#modelmismatch): The guard model was built for another version of the code.
- [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged): The PDF changed on disk while it was being read.
- [`Cancelled`](errors.md#cancelled): The `cancel` token was set. Pages already read stay in the cache.

> **Note**
>
> The OCR workers are started with the `spawn` method, so they import your main script again. Put every call
> to `extract.read` (and to `Reader`) under `if __name__ == "__main__":`. Without the guard, a read that needs a
> worker (a scanned PDF) raises [`EngineLoadError`](errors.md#engineloaderror) with `cause="no_main_guard"` after a few seconds, and the
> worker prints one line on stderr. A digital PDF needs no worker and reads fine even without the guard, so
> the fault shows only on scans.
>
> With the default `Options.processes`, `read` starts up to two worker processes of about 1.5 GB each: do not
> run two reads at once on a small machine.

**Example**

```python
import extract

if __name__ == "__main__":
    doc = extract.read("invoice.pdf", extract.Options(work_dir="work"))
    print(doc.status, len(doc.doubtful()))
```

```text
# output
done 3
```

**See also**: [`Reader`](reader.md#reader), [`Options`](options.md#options), [`load`](#load), [`inspect`](#inspect), [`CancelToken`](#canceltoken), [`Document`](document.md#document).

## `load`

```text
load(path: str | Path, source: str | Path | None = None, options: Options | None = None) -> Document
```

Open a saved reading, a `.extract.json` file, as a [`Document`](document.md#document), without reading anything again.

`load` is the way back from [`Document.save`](document.md#documentsave) or from the `json` export. It runs no OCR and loads no model, so it
takes well under a second, and the result is equal (`==`) to the document that was saved. It reads files of schema
version 2 and the older version 1. The PDF is needed only for [`Document.page_image`](document.md#documentpage_image), [`Document.word_crop`](document.md#documentword_crop) and the
`pdf` export.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| Path` | required | The saved reading. |
| `source` | `str \| Path \| None` | `None` | The PDF the reading was made from. By default `load` looks for the file with the name recorded in the JSON in the same folder as the JSON, and uses it if it exists. Pass `source` when the PDF is somewhere else. |
| `options` | `Options \| None` | `None` | Used only for `work_dir`, where later corrections are logged, and for `languages` when the file has none. The default `Options()` logs into the default work folder (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/extract`, else `~/.cache/extract`), so pass `Options(work_dir=...)` when you will correct the loaded document. |

**Returns**

The `Document`. Its `source` is `None` if no PDF was found. A PDF whose hash differs from the one recorded is not detected here: [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged) is raised when you first use it (`page_image`, `word_crop`, the `pdf` export).

**Raises**

- `FileNotFoundError`: `path` does not exist. This is the built-in exception, not an [`ExtractError`](errors.md#extracterror).
- [`UnsupportedFile`](errors.md#unsupportedfile): The file is not JSON, or it is JSON that is not an Extract document of schema version 1 or 2.
- `KeyError`: The file declares a supported schema version but lacks fields (a damaged or hand-edited file).

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json")
print(doc.name, doc.source)

elsewhere = extract.load("invoice.extract.json", source="scans/invoice.pdf")
print(elsewhere.source)
```

```text
# output
invoice.pdf invoice.pdf
scans/invoice.pdf
```

**See also**: [`Document.save`](document.md#documentsave), [`Document.export`](document.md#documentexport), [`read`](#read), [`Options`](options.md#options).

## `inspect`

```text
inspect(path: str | Path) -> FileInfo
```

Say how many pages a PDF has and whether it is digital, scanned or mixed, without reading it.

It opens the PDF, looks at each page's text layer and images, and closes it, with no OCR and no model. A page
counts as digital when its text layer has at least 80 characters that are not spaces and no image covers half the
page or more; any other page, a blank one included, counts as scanned. The quality of a text layer is judged later,
when the document is read.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| Path` | required | The PDF, as a string or a `Path`. |

**Returns**

A [`FileInfo`](#fileinfo) with the page counts, the kind and the file size.

**Raises**

- `FileNotFoundError`: `path` does not exist. This is the built-in exception, not an [`ExtractError`](errors.md#extracterror).
- [`UnsupportedFile`](errors.md#unsupportedfile): The file is not a PDF that can be opened. The error carries `file=`.
- [`PasswordProtected`](errors.md#passwordprotected): The PDF needs a password to be opened. The error carries `file=`. A PDF that has only an owner password (restrictions on printing or copying) opens normally.

**Example**

```python
import extract

info = extract.inspect("scans/damaged.pdf")
print(info.kind, info.pages, info.size)
```

```text
# output
scanned 3 41019
```

**See also**: [`FileInfo`](#fileinfo), [`read`](#read).

## `FileInfo`

What [`inspect`](#inspect) learns about a PDF without reading any page with OCR.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `Path` | The path that was inspected, as a `Path`. |
| `pages` | `int` | Number of pages. |
| `kind` | `str` | `digital` when every page has a text layer and no scanned image, `scanned` when none does, `mixed` otherwise. See `inspect` for the exact rule. |
| `size` | `int` | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `scanned_pages` | `int` | Pages that count as scanned and would need OCR. |
| `digital_pages` | `int` | Pages that have a text layer long enough to be used as it is. `scanned_pages` plus `digital_pages` is always `pages`. |

## `CancelToken`

A switch that stops a running [`read`](#read) or `export` from another thread, or from its own event callback.

Create one, pass it as `cancel=`, and call `cancel()` when the job should stop. A read stops within about two
seconds, raises [`Cancelled`](errors.md#cancelled) and sends `Finished("stopped")`. Pages that were already read stay in the page cache,
so reading the same file again starts where this read stopped. A token cannot be reset: make a new one for the
next job.

**Example**

```python
import threading

import extract

if __name__ == "__main__":
    token = extract.CancelToken()
    threading.Timer(0.5, token.cancel).start()
    try:
        extract.read("invoice.pdf", extract.Options(work_dir="cancel-work"), cancel=token)
    except extract.Cancelled:
        print("stopped")
```

```text
# output
stopped
```

**See also**: [`read`](#read), [`Reader.read`](reader.md#readerread), [`Document.export`](document.md#documentexport), [`Cancelled`](errors.md#cancelled).

### `CancelToken.cancel`

```text
CancelToken.cancel() -> None
```

Ask the job that holds this token to stop.

Safe to call from any thread, and more than once. The job notices within about two seconds; it does not
return anything here.

### `CancelToken.is_set`

```text
CancelToken.is_set() -> bool
```

Return True once `cancel` has been called.

**Returns**

Whether the token has been cancelled.

---

[Back to the reference index](index.md); next: [Reader](reader.md).

# docs/reference/reader.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# Reader

`Reader` keeps the OCR workers and the models loaded between documents: use it whenever you read more than one file.

## `Reader`

```text
Reader(options: Options | None = None, *, guard: Any = None, lexicon: Any = None)
```

Worker processes and models kept loaded between reads, so that a batch pays the start-up cost once.

[`read`](functions.md#read) starts the workers for each call and stops them at the end; a `Reader` keeps them. Nothing is loaded when
you create it: the first `read` loads the word lists, the guard and the OCR engine, and a missing piece raises
[`EngineLoadError`](errors.md#engineloaderror) there. Use it as a context manager, so that the workers stop when the block ends.

A `Reader` reads one document at a time. Do not call [`Reader.read`](#readerread) from several threads at once; use one `Reader`
per process or serialise the calls.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | `Options \| None` | `None` | The [`Options`](options.md#options) of every read made with this `Reader`. The default is `Options()`. |
| `guard` | `Any` | `None` | Which guard judges the words. `None` loads the packaged guard model (the file named by `$EXTRACT_GUARD_MODEL` if that variable is set; `"thorough"` second reading uses its own model). `False` reads without a guard: every OCR word comes out `unscored` and each page sends `guard.warning.unscored` with the cause `no_guard`. Any other object with an `info` attribute and a `score_page(...)` method is used as a custom guard; that is for tests and research, not for normal use. Keyword-only. |
| `lexicon` | `Any` | `None` | The word lists the guard compares against. `None` loads the packaged lists for `Options.languages`, `False` uses none, and any other object with the methods `has` and `share` is used as the lists. Keyword-only. |

**Attributes**

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `options` | The `Options` this reader was made with. |

> **Note**
>
> As with `read`, the workers import your main script again: create the `Reader` under
> `if __name__ == "__main__":`. With the default `Options.processes`, at most two worker processes run, and a
> `Reader` can use about 1.5 GB of memory for each.

**Example**

```python
import extract

if __name__ == "__main__":
    options = extract.Options(work_dir="work")
    with extract.Reader(options) as reader:
        for name in ("scan.pdf", "invoice.pdf"):
            doc = reader.read(name)
            print(name, doc.status, len(doc.doubtful()))
```

```text
# output
scan.pdf done 0
invoice.pdf done 3
```

**See also**: [`read`](functions.md#read), [`Options`](options.md#options), [`Reader.read`](#readerread), [`Reader.close`](#readerclose).

### `Reader.job_log`

Property, `list[dict[str, Any]]`.

What the engine decided and measured while this [`Reader`](#reader) worked, as a list of dictionaries.

Each entry has a `code` such as `ram.workers` (how many workers the free memory allows), `worker.started`,
`worker.ready` (with the seconds the models took to load), `pool.page` (a page read by a worker),
`worker.died` or `worker.recycled`. The list is a copy and is empty before the first [`read`](functions.md#read). The same entries
are appended, one JSON line each, to `job.log` in the work folder.

Every entry has a `time` and a `code`, and the other keys depend on the code: the `ram.workers` entry has
`free_mb`, `budget_mb`, `processes`, `threads` and `backend`, among others. Pages that come from the page cache
need no worker, so a read of cached pages leaves the list empty.

### `Reader.read`

```text
Reader.read(
    path: str | Path,
    on_event: Callable[[Event], None] | None = None,
    cancel: CancelToken | None = None,
    *,
    correct: str | None = None,
) -> Document
```

Read one PDF with the workers and models this [`Reader`](#reader) already holds.

This is what [`extract.read`](functions.md#read) does, without starting and stopping the workers around it, and it raises what `read`
raises. A page that was read before with the same file, resolution and engine comes from the page cache in the
work folder and costs no OCR. A page that cannot be read is not an exception: the document comes back `partial`.
Each call sends its own events, from [`Started`](events.md#started) to [`Finished`](events.md#finished); see `events`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| Path` | required | The PDF, as a string or a `Path`. |
| `on_event` | `Callable[[Event], None] \| None` | `None` | A function called with each [`Event`](events.md#event). It runs in the thread that called `read`, so it can call `cancel.cancel()` itself. |
| `cancel` | `CancelToken \| None` | `None` | A [`CancelToken`](functions.md#canceltoken) to stop the read from another thread or from `on_event`. |
| `correct` | `str \| None` | `None` | `off`, `safe` or `more`, overriding [`Options.correct`](options.md#options) for this document only. `None` uses the option. Keyword-only. |

**Returns**

The [`Document`](document.md#document).

> **Note**
>
> Every failure inside the read, and [`Cancelled`](errors.md#cancelled), send `Finished` (`"failed"` or `"stopped"`) before the
> exception leaves. Errors found before the read starts (a bad `correct`, models or word lists that cannot
> be loaded) send no `Finished`. One read at a time per `Reader`.

### `Reader.close`

```text
Reader.close() -> None
```

Stop the worker processes and the second-reading process.

The OCR models live in the workers and go with them. Leaving a `with` block calls it. The [`Reader`](#reader) is still
usable afterwards: the next [`read`](functions.md#read) prepares everything again. Calling it twice, or before any `read`, does
nothing.

---

[Back to the reference index](index.md); next: [Document](document.md).

# docs/reference/document.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# Document

`Document` is what a read returns and what `load` gives back: pages, words, numbers and invoice fields, with the methods that review, correct, save and export them. The class comes first, then its properties and methods.

## `Document`

A document that has been read: its pages and words with their status, its numbers and its invoice fields.

You do not build a `Document`. [`read`](functions.md#read) and [`Reader.read`](reader.md#readerread) return one after reading a PDF, and [`load`](functions.md#load) returns one
from a saved reading (a `.extract.json` file).

What you read from it (`pages`, `numbers`, `invoice`, `word`) is a snapshot of the present state. What you change
(`correct`, `accept`, `use_suggestion`, `reopen`, `set_mode`, `undo`) makes a new snapshot and runs the number
rules that the change can affect again. The words themselves are immutable objects: after a change, ask for the word
again, because a [`Word`](data-types.md#word) you already hold keeps its old values. Every method that takes a word id, such as `"p1w13"`,
raises `KeyError` when no word of the document has that id.

Two documents are equal (`==`) when the JSON they would save is the same: pages, words, numbers, invoice, options and
corrections. A document loaded from a save of another is equal to it. A `Document` is not hashable.

**Attributes**

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | The PDF the document was read from, as a `Path`, or `None` for a document from `load` whose PDF was not found. Without it you can still read, correct and save, and export to `xlsx`, `json` and `txt`; `page_image`, `word_crop` and the `pdf` export raise [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged). |

> **Note**
>
> The methods that change the document hold a lock, so changes from several threads never interleave. The reading
> methods take no lock: do not read from one thread while another changes the same document. Every `correct`,
> `accept`, `use_suggestion`, `reopen`, `undo` and `set_mode` appends one line to `corrections.jsonl` in the work
> folder ([`Options.work_dir`](options.md#options); by default `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/extract`, else `~/.cache/extract`); `undo_page` and
> `undo_all` write nothing there. A document from `load` writes there too: pass `Options(work_dir=...)` to `load`
> to choose the folder. Nothing is written for a change that raises.

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json", options=extract.Options(work_dir="work"))
print(doc.name, doc.status, len(doc.pages))
for word in doc.doubtful():
    print(word.id, word.text, round(word.p_wrong, 2), word.suggestion)
doc.accept("p1w11")
doc.correct("p1w13", "Esquivar")
word = doc.word("p1w13")
print(word.text, word.status, word.review, word.original, len(doc.doubtful()))
```

```text
# output
invoice.pdf done 1
p1w11 Pelmuda 0.19 None
p1w13 Esquilmar 0.12 Esquivar
p1w4 F-2026-0498 0.04 None
Esquivar doubtful corrected Esquilmar 1
```

**See also**: [`read`](functions.md#read), [`load`](functions.md#load), [`Word`](data-types.md#word), [`Page`](data-types.md#page-pagereading), [`Number`](data-types.md#number-numberresult), [`Invoice`](data-types.md#invoice-invoicefields).

### `Document.name`

Property, `str`.

The file name of the PDF the document was read from, such as `invoice.pdf`. No folder is included.

### `Document.sha256`

Property, `str`.

SHA-256 of the source PDF, as 64 hexadecimal digits.

A saved reading records it, and the methods that need the PDF use it to refuse a different file.

### `Document.doc_id`

Property, `str`.

The first 12 hexadecimal digits of `sha256`: the id that events and the interface use for this document.

### `Document.status`

Property, `str`.

`done`, or `partial` when at least one page could not be read (see `unreadable_pages`).

A `partial` document is returned, not raised: check this value after every read.

### `Document.unreadable_pages`

Property, `tuple[int, ...]`.

The numbers of the pages that could not be read, 1-based, in page order. `()` when there is none.

Each such page has the status `unreadable`, and its [`Page.reason`](data-types.md#page-pagereading) says why. Its words are kept as `unscored`,
and no number on it is ever `checked`.

### `Document.pages`

Property, `tuple[PageReading, ...]`.

The pages in order; page 1 is at index 0.

Each [`Page`](data-types.md#page-pagereading) holds its words with their status and corrections.

### `Document.numbers`

Property, `tuple[NumberResult, ...]`.

Every number of the document with its status, in reading order. See [`Number`](data-types.md#number-numberresult).

### `Document.invoice`

Property, `InvoiceFields | None`.

The fields and lines of an invoice, or None when `doc_type` is `generic`.

Only page 1 is read for fields. A field that was not found is `None` inside the [`Invoice`](data-types.md#invoice-invoicefields), never a guess.

### `Document.doc_type`

Property, `str`.

`invoice` or `generic`.

A document is an `invoice` when page 1 has an invoice title near the top and at least two totals labels, such
as the base, the VAT and the total. Anything else is `generic`, and [`Document.invoice`](#documentinvoice) is then `None`.

### `Document.locale`

Property, `str | None`.

`es` or `en`: how the amounts of the document are written (`1.234,56` or `1,234.56`).

It is decided from the numbers themselves and the number rules rest on it. `Options.languages[0]` breaks a
tie. It is `None` only for a document loaded from a file that had no locale.

### `Document.mode`

Property, `str`.

The correction mode the document is in: `off`, `safe` or `more`.

It is the mode the read used, or the one last given to `set_mode`.

### `Document.page_notes`

Property, `list[dict[str, Any]]`.

What the read noticed about pages whose text may not be what is printed, though nothing was changed.

Each note is a dictionary: `{"key": "page.warning.low_resolution", "page": 2, "dpi": 80}` for a scan under 100
dpi (read at 100 dpi; `dpi` is its real resolution), and `{"key": "page.warning.sideways", "page": 2}` when the
lines run up or down. The list is a copy, empty when there is nothing to say, and the JSON keeps it under
`options.page_notes`.

### `Document.fixes`

Property, `dict[str, Any]`.

A summary of what the guard changed, as a dictionary.

The keys are `mode`, `second_reading` (bool), `thorough` (bool), `applied` and `undone` (counts),
`by_source` and `by_op` (counts by the source and the operation of each fix), `withheld` (the pages where the
fixes were held back: a list of `{"page": 1, "share": 0.12}`) and `second_reading_failed_pages` (the pages that
did not get their second reading).

### `Document.word`

```text
Document.word(word_id: str) -> Word
```

Return the present state of a word, with its text after any correction.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word_id` | `str` | required | The id of the word, such as `"p3w17"` (page 3, word 17: the page counts from 1 and the word from 0, in reading order). A token id such as `"p3w17#1"` is accepted and gives the word it belongs to. |

**Returns**

The [`Word`](data-types.md#word). Ask again after a change: a word you already hold is not updated.

### `Document.words`

```text
Document.words() -> Iterator[Word]
```

Iterate over every word of every page, in reading order.

**Returns**

An iterator of [`Word`](data-types.md#word). Words that a guard fix joined into another stay in the sequence with the text `""` and the status `absorbed`.

### `Document.doubtful`

```text
Document.doubtful() -> list[Word]
```

List the words that still need a decision, the likeliest to be wrong first.

A word is listed when nobody has decided it (`review` is `None`) and its status is `doubtful` or `unscored`.
The `doubtful` words come first, by falling `p_wrong`; the `unscored` words come after them, in reading order.
A word the user accepted or corrected leaves the list, although its `status` does not change.

`unscored` means that nobody could judge the word: there was no guard, the page was unreadable, or the guard
had no confidence to work with. These words are in the list on purpose. To keep only the words the guard
flagged, filter on the status.

**Returns**

A new list of [`Word`](data-types.md#word). Empty when there is nothing to decide.

### `Document.fixed`

```text
Document.fixed() -> list[Word]
```

List the words that carry a fix the guard applied, in reading order.

These are the first word of a join, a segmented word, a changed word and a dropped word. With the correction
mode `off` (the default) the list is empty.

**Returns**

A new list of [`Word`](data-types.md#word).

### `Document.fix_info`

```text
Document.fix_info(word_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None
```

Return the guard's proposal for a word, applied or not, as the saved JSON carries it.

**Returns**

A dictionary with the keys `op`, `kind`, `text`, `ids`, `source`, `sources`, `p_fix`, `p_keep`, `rule`, `modes`, `reasons` and `applied`, or `None` when the word has no proposal. `modes` lists the correction modes that apply it; an empty list means the proposal is shown but never applied. See [`Fix`](data-types.md#fix).

### `Document.field_status`

```text
Document.field_status(cell: Cell | None) -> str
```

Return how far a field of the invoice can be trusted.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cell` | `Cell \| None` | required | A field of [`Document.invoice`](#documentinvoice), such as `doc.invoice.total`, or `None` for a field the invoice does not have. |

**Returns**

`mismatch` if any number made of the cell's words is `mismatch`, else `checked` if one of them is `checked`, else `unverified`. `None` gives `unverified`.

### `Document.correct`

```text
Document.correct(word_id: str, text: str) -> None
```

Replace the text of a word with the text you typed.

The OCR text stays in [`Word.original`](data-types.md#word) (from the first correction on: a second correction does not overwrite
it). The word gets `review="corrected"` and `corrected_by="user"`, its `suggestion` is cleared, and the number
rules that cover the word run again. The word's `status` does not change, and it leaves [`Document.doubtful`](#documentdoubtful). A
corrected number becomes `checked` only if a verifying rule passes with the new text.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word_id` | `str` | required | The id of the word, such as `"p1w13"`. |
| `text` | `str` | required | The new text of the word, exactly as it should appear. |

### `Document.accept`

```text
Document.accept(word_id: str) -> None
```

Confirm that a word is right as it stands.

Any word can be accepted, not only the doubtful ones. The word gets `review="accepted"` and leaves
[`Document.doubtful`](#documentdoubtful). Its `status` stays as it was, so an accepted word can still have the status `doubtful`: test
`review` to know whether somebody decided. Accepting never makes a number `checked`: only the rules do that.

> **Note**
>
> Accepting a word you had corrected turns `corrected` into `accepted` and keeps the text you typed;
> [`Document.reopen`](#documentreopen) then clears the decision but does not restore the OCR text. Decide each word once.

### `Document.use_suggestion`

```text
Document.use_suggestion(word_id: str) -> None
```

Apply the suggestion that a word carries, as a correction by the user.

When the word has a suggestion of its own ([`Word.suggestion`](data-types.md#word), the guard's plain text change), that one is
applied; only when it has none is the one-digit fix of its [`Number`](data-types.md#number-numberresult) ([`DigitSuggestion`](data-types.md#digitsuggestion)) used. The change goes through
`correct`. A digit
suggestion exists only when exactly one single-digit change makes the failing rule pass, so a tie gives none (common
for IBANs), and a number written in several words (an IBAN in groups of four) never gets one that this method can
apply: correct the word that holds the wrong digit.

It applies whatever is offered. A word suggestion can have a small `Word.suggestion_conf`, and a digit change can
have `DigitSuggestion.verified` false: look at [`Document.word_crop`](#documentword_crop) and those two values before you call it.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: The word has no suggestion to apply.

### `Document.reopen`

```text
Document.reopen(word_id: str) -> None
```

Take back a decision you made on a word.

An accepted word becomes undecided and is in [`Document.doubtful`](#documentdoubtful) again. A corrected word gets the text it was
read with, `original` and `corrected_by` are cleared, and the number rules that cover it run again.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: The word is neither accepted nor corrected, or it is a corrected word that carries a guard fix (use `undo` for it).

### `Document.tokens`

```text
Document.tokens(page: int) -> tuple[Word, ...]
```

Return the words of a page as the text layer and the number rules see them.

Absorbed words are gone and a word the guard segmented is split into tokens whose ids have the form `"p3w17#1"`.
[`Document.word`](#documentword) accepts a token id and gives the word it comes from.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `int` | required | The page number, counting from 1. |

**Returns**

The tokens of the page, in reading order, as [`Word`](data-types.md#word) objects.

**Raises**

- `IndexError`: `page` is larger than the number of pages.

> **Note**
>
> The low end is not checked: `0` returns the last page and `-1` the one before it, as a list index does.

### `Document.set_mode`

```text
Document.set_mode(mode: str) -> None
```

Change the correction mode of the document without reading it again.

The guard's stored proposals are applied again for `mode`. Words that a user decided never move, and a page
where the fixes would change more than 8 % of its words keeps none (the pages held back are in
`Document.fixes["withheld"]`). `off` takes every applied fix back, so the text is that of an `off` read.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `str` | required | `off`, `safe` or `more`, as for [`Options.correct`](options.md#options). Arithmetic digit fixes are applied only in `more`. |

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: `mode` is not one of the three.

### `Document.undo`

```text
Document.undo(word_id: str) -> None
```

Take back the guard's fix of a word, or of the group of words it belongs to.

Pass the id of a word that carries an applied fix, such as the owner of a join. The text, id, box and status of
the words come back as they were read. The word counts as decided (`review="accepted"`), so a later `set_mode`
does not apply the fix again. The proposal stays on the word and `fix_info` still shows it.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: The word has no applied fix.

### `Document.undo_page`

```text
Document.undo_page(number: int) -> int
```

Take back every fix the guard applied on one page.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `number` | `int` | required | The page number, counting from 1. |

**Returns**

How many fixes were undone. 0 when the page has none.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: The document has no such page.

### `Document.undo_all`

```text
Document.undo_all() -> int
```

Take back every fix the guard applied in the document.

The text is then exactly that of the `off` read. Words you corrected or accepted yourself stay as you left
them.

**Returns**

How many fixes were undone. 0 when there are none.

### `Document.save`

```text
Document.save(path: str | Path) -> None
```

Write the document as a saved reading, a `.extract.json` file, that [`load`](functions.md#load) reads back.

The file holds every page, word, number and invoice field with its status, and every correction made so far.
Its fields are described in [JSON format](json-format.md). The PDF is not part of it.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| Path` | required | The file to write. Its folder must exist. By convention the name ends in `.extract.json`. |

**Raises**

- `OSError`: The file cannot be written (a missing folder, no permission, a full disk).

> **Note**
>
> `save` overwrites an existing file without asking and does not check what it wrote; `export` with
> `formats=("json",)` never replaces anything and checks the file.

### `Document.export`

```text
Document.export(
    destination: str | Path,
    formats: Sequence[str] = ("pdf", "xlsx", "json", "txt"),
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    language: str = "en",
    on_event: Callable[[Event], None] | None = None,
    cancel: CancelToken | None = None,
) -> list[Path]
```

Write the document as a searchable PDF, a workbook, a JSON file and a text file.

Nothing is read again and no model is loaded, so exporting after corrections is cheap, and the files hold the
corrections made so far. Every file is written under a hidden temporary name, checked (the PDF has the same number
of pages, the JSON reads back equal, the workbook has its sheets, the text reads back as written) and only then
given its final name.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `destination` | `str \| Path` | required | The folder to write into. It is created if it does not exist. |
| `formats` | `Sequence[str]` | `("pdf", "xlsx", "json", "txt")` | Which files to write, from `"pdf"` (`<name>.searchable.pdf`), `"xlsx"` (`<name>.xlsx`), `"json"` (`<name>.extract.json`) and `"txt"` (`<name>.txt`). The default is all four, in that order. |
| `name` | `str \| None` | `None` | The name shared by the files, without extension. The default is the stem of the PDF's name. Keyword-only. |
| `language` | `str` | `"en"` | `"en"` or `"es"`: the language of the reasons and rule texts in the workbook. Any other value makes the workbook show the message keys and their values instead of sentences. Keyword-only. |
| `on_event` | `Callable[[Event], None] \| None` | `None` | A function called, in the thread that called `export`, with `Warning("export.warning.unreadable_text_layer", ...)` when unreadable pages still get their few words into the PDF text layer, and with [`Exported`](events.md#exported) once everything is written. Keyword-only. |
| `cancel` | `CancelToken \| None` | `None` | A [`CancelToken`](functions.md#canceltoken). It is looked at between formats only, not inside one. Keyword-only. |

**Returns**

The paths of the files written, in the order of `formats`.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: A name in `formats` is not one of the four, or a file failed its check after writing.
- [`OutputExists`](errors.md#outputexists): `destination` is a file, or the name and its numbered copies `name-2` to `name-999` are all taken.
- [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged): `"pdf"` was asked for and the source PDF is missing ([`Document.source`](#document) is `None`) or is not the file the document was read from (its hash differs). The other formats do not need the PDF.
- [`Cancelled`](errors.md#cancelled): The `cancel` token was set before a format was written.

> **Note**
>
> A taken name is never overwritten: the whole set takes the first free copy number (`invoice-2.xlsx`,
> `invoice-2.txt`, ...), so the files of one export always match. A file that fails its check or is interrupted
> is removed; formats already finished keep their names. The searchable PDF keeps the original pages and adds an
> invisible text layer in WinAnsi encoding (other characters become `?` in the layer only), and it has no owner
> password even when the source had one.

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json")
paths = doc.export("export-example", ("xlsx", "txt"))
print([path.name for path in paths])
again = doc.export("export-example", ("xlsx", "txt"))
print([path.name for path in again])
```

```text
# output
['invoice.xlsx', 'invoice.txt']
['invoice-2.xlsx', 'invoice-2.txt']
```

### `Document.page_image`

```text
Document.page_image(number: int, zoom: float = 1.0) -> bytes
```

Return a page as a PNG image, drawn from the source PDF.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `number` | `int` | required | The page number, counting from 1. |
| `zoom` | `float` | `1.0` | A factor on the page's own resolution: the image is drawn at `round(dpi * zoom)` dpi, where `dpi` is [`Page.dpi`](data-types.md#page-pagereading). 1.0 gives the pixel grid that the word boxes use. Use 0.5 for a thumbnail. |

**Returns**

The PNG file as bytes.

**Raises**

- [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged): The source PDF is missing ([`Document.source`](#document) is `None`) or is not the file the document was read from.
- `IndexError`: `number` is larger than the number of pages.

> **Note**
>
> Each call opens the PDF and draws the page again, under a lock shared by the whole process: keep the
> result if you need it twice. `0` is the last page, as for `tokens`.

### `Document.word_crop`

```text
Document.word_crop(word_id: str, pad: int = 8) -> bytes
```

Return the picture of one word as a PNG image, cut from the page.

This is what a reviewer needs to compare a doubtful word with the print: the word's box ([`Word.box`](data-types.md#word), in pixels
of the page at its own resolution), made larger on every side.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word_id` | `str` | required | The id of the word, such as `"p1w13"`. |
| `pad` | `int` | `8` | Pixels added on every side of the word's box. 0 gives the box alone. The crop never goes outside the page. |

**Returns**

The PNG file as bytes.

**Raises**

- [`SourceChanged`](errors.md#sourcechanged): The source PDF is missing ([`Document.source`](#document) is `None`) or is not the file the document was read from.

> **Note**
>
> Each call opens the PDF and draws the whole page before it cuts, under a lock shared by the whole process.

# docs/reference/options.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# Options

`Options` holds every setting of a read. Every field has a default, so `Options()` is a valid choice.

## `Options`

The settings of a read, as one immutable object.

Make one with the fields you want to change; the others keep their defaults. Pass it to [`read`](functions.md#read), to [`Reader`](reader.md#reader), and
to [`load`](functions.md#load) (which uses only `work_dir` and `languages`). The object is frozen: to change a setting, make a new
`Options`, for instance with `dataclasses.replace`. Every field is checked when the object is made.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `languages` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `("es", "en")` | The languages of the documents, a non-empty subset of `("es", "en")`. They choose the word lists the guard compares each word with, and the first one breaks a tie when the style of the amounts (`1.234,56` or `1,234.56`) cannot be decided from the numbers. A list is turned into a tuple. A plain string such as `"es"` is refused: write `("es",)`. The OCR models are the same for both languages. On a page in a language you did not choose, the guard applies no fix and sends `guard.warning.fixes_withheld`. |
| `review` | `str` | `"balanced"` | How many words the guard flags as `doubtful`: `"fewer"`, `"balanced"` (the default) or `"more"`, each a fixed threshold set on the development pages so that about 3 %, 5 % and 8 % of their words are flagged. It is not a share of each page: a damaged page gets more flags and a clean page almost none. `"fewer"` asks you to check less and lets more wrong words through; `"more"` does the opposite. |
| `recycle_pages` | `int` | `120` | How many pages an OCR worker reads before it is replaced by a fresh one, at least 4. The default is 120. A worker is also replaced earlier when its memory grows past about 1.4 GB (1.3 GB on a small machine). Lower it on a machine with little memory. |
| `work_dir` | `Path \| str \| None` | `None` | The work folder: the page cache, `job.log` and `corrections.jsonl`. A string is turned into a `Path`. `None` (the default) means `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/extract` if that variable is set, else `~/.cache/extract`. Deleting the folder removes every trace of the reads. The interface always uses `~/.cache/extract` and ignores `XDG_CACHE_HOME`. |
| `processes` | `int \| None` | `None` | How many OCR worker processes to run, at least 1. `None` (the default) chooses from the free memory and the physical cores, with a maximum of 2. Each process is planned at about 1.5 GB with the OpenVINO backend (the largest worker measured used 1,330 MB) and 700 MB with `onnxruntime`. |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | `None` | How many threads each worker uses, at least 1. `None` (the default) is the number of physical cores divided by `processes`, and at least 1. |
| `backend` | `str` | `"auto"` | The engine that runs the OCR: `"auto"` (the default), `"openvino"` or `"onnxruntime"`. `"auto"` picks OpenVINO when more than 2,000 MB are free and `onnxruntime` otherwise. Asking for `"openvino"` when the workers start another backend raises [`EngineLoadError`](errors.md#engineloaderror). |
| `correct` | `str` | `"off"` | How far the guard may change words: `"off"` (the default) changes nothing, `"safe"` applies the fixes of the strictest precision and `"more"` those with the best net balance; every fix can be undone. A page whose fixes would change more than 8 % of its words keeps none, and a digit changes only when a verifying rule confirms it (the arithmetic rules only in `"more"`). `read` can override this field for one document. |
| `second_reading` | `bool \| str` | `False` | Whether to read the doubtful lines again with other recognisers, in a separate process: `False` (the default in 5.0.7), `True` or the exact string `"thorough"`. `0` and `1` are refused. With `True` the readings are computed, but the packaged guard model was trained without them, so it ignores them and each page sends `guard.warning.readings_differ`: that costs time and memory and changes nothing. `"thorough"` reads 16 lines with the two light recognisers and 40 zones with the deep one, judged by its own guard model; it adds 2.95 s a page on average on 60 pilot pages and a reader process of up to 1.6 GB. It needs the extra reader models (`python3 scripts/fetch_models.py --all`); without them the read raises `EngineLoadError`. |

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: A field is out of range. The message names the field and the valid values: `languages` is empty or holds anything but `"es"` and `"en"`; `review`, `backend` or `correct` is not one of its values; `second_reading` is not `True`, `False` or `"thorough"`; `recycle_pages` is under 4; `processes` or `threads` is under 1.
- `dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError`: You assigned to a field of an existing `Options`.

**Example**

```python
import extract

options = extract.Options(languages=("es",), review="more", work_dir="work")
print(options.languages, options.review, options.correct, options.thorough)

try:
    extract.Options(review="most")
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)
```

```text
# output
('es',) more off False
review must be one of ('fewer', 'balanced', 'more'), got 'most'
```

**See also**: [`read`](functions.md#read), [`Reader`](reader.md#reader), [`load`](functions.md#load), [`Document.set_mode`](document.md#documentset_mode).

### `Options.thorough`

Property, `bool`.

True when `second_reading` is the exact string `"thorough"`, and only then.

`True` is not thorough: it selects the default second reading.

---

[Back to the reference index](index.md); next: [Data types](data-types.md).

# docs/reference/data-types.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# Data types

The objects you read from a `Document`. They are frozen: a change goes through a method of the `Document`, which gives new objects. `Page`, `Number`, `Rule` and `Invoice` are the short public names of `PageReading`, `NumberResult`, `RuleResult` and `InvoiceFields`.

## `Word`

One word of a page, with what the engine and the guard know about it.

A `Word` is a snapshot. A [`Document`](document.md#document) replaces it when you correct or accept it, so ask [`Document.word`](document.md#documentword) again to
see the change.

The `status` says how far to trust the word as read: `ok` means that the guard looked at the word and did not
flag it, not that the word is verified, and `unscored` means that nobody could judge it. Your decisions do not change
`status`: they set `review`, so a word you accepted can still be `doubtful`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | `p{page}w{index}`: the page counts from 1, the index from 0 in reading order. `"p3w17"` is the 18th word of page 3. Token ids such as `"p3w17#1"` exist only in [`Document.tokens`](document.md#documenttokens). |
| `page` | `int` | The page number, counting from 1. |
| `text` | `str` | The current text: what was read, or what a fix or a correction made of it. Empty for an `absorbed` word. |
| `box` | `Box` | `(left, top, right, bottom)` in pixels of the page as drawn at [`Page.dpi`](#page-pagereading). |
| `conf` | `float \| None` | The OCR confidence of the word itself, from 0 to 1: the mean of its characters' confidences. For an unaligned word (see `Page.unaligned_words`) it is the mean of the word's line. `None` on `native` pages. |
| `char_conf` | `tuple[float, ...] \| None` | One confidence per character, or `None` on `native` pages and for words whose characters could not be told apart from their line's (`Page.unaligned_words`). |
| `line_id` | `int` | The number of the text line the word is on, from 0. |
| `idx_in_line` | `int` | The position of the word inside its line, from 0. |
| `status` | `str` | `native` (from the PDF's text layer, not scored), `ok`, `doubtful`, `fixed` (the owner of a fix the guard applied), `absorbed` (joined into another word or dropped by a fix) or `unscored`. |
| `p_wrong` | `float \| None` | The guard's calibrated probability that the word is wrong, or `None` for `native` and `unscored` words. |
| `reasons` | `tuple[Reason, ...]` | Why the word is doubtful, as [`Reason`](#reason) objects, in the order the guard lists them. |
| `suggestion` | `str \| None` | A replacement text, set only on a `doubtful` word whose proposed fix is a plain change of text. [`Document.use_suggestion`](document.md#documentuse_suggestion) applies it. |
| `suggestion_conf` | `float \| None` | The probability that the suggestion is right ([`Fix.p_fix`](#fix)), which can be small. |
| `review` | `str \| None` | `None` while nobody has decided, `"accepted"` after [`Document.accept`](document.md#documentaccept), `"corrected"` after [`Document.correct`](document.md#documentcorrect). A word with a `review` is not in [`Document.doubtful`](document.md#documentdoubtful). |
| `original` | `str \| None` | The text before the first correction or applied fix, or `None`. |
| `corrected_by` | `str \| None` | `"guard"` for an applied fix, `"user"` for a correction, `None` otherwise. |
| `char_alts` | `tuple[tuple[tuple[str, float], ...], ...] \| None` | For each character, the recogniser's alternatives as `(character, probability)` pairs. Engine detail, not saved in the JSON. |
| `masked` | `str \| None` | The reading of the word with a restricted alphabet, used as evidence by the guard. Engine detail, not saved. |
| `readings` | `tuple[Reading, ...] \| None` | The second readings of the word, as [`Reading`](#reading) objects, or `None`. Engine detail, not saved. |
| `fix` | `Fix \| None` | The guard's proposal as a `Fix`, applied or not, or `None`. |
| `absorbed_by` | `str \| None` | The id of the word that took this one in, for an `absorbed` word. |
| `guard_status` | `str \| None` | The status the guard gave the word before a fix changed it; [`Document.undo`](document.md#documentundo) restores it. |
| `orig_box` | `Box \| None` | The box the word had before a join widened it; `Document.undo` restores it. |

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json")
word = doc.word("p1w13")
print(word.id, word.text, word.status, round(word.p_wrong, 2), word.reasons[0].key)
```

```text
# output
p1w13 Esquilmar doubtful 0.12 guard.reason.not_in_dictionary
```

**See also**: [`Document.word`](document.md#documentword), [`Document.doubtful`](document.md#documentdoubtful), [`Page`](#page-pagereading), [`Fix`](#fix), [`Reason`](#reason).

## `Page` (`PageReading`)

`extract.Page` is the class `PageReading`; `repr` and tracebacks show the long name.

What the engine gives for one page: its size, its status and its words.

A page is `unreadable` when fewer than 25 words came out (`page.reason.few_words`), when the mean confidence is
under 0.65 (`page.reason.low_confidence`), or when it could not be drawn or its worker died twice
(`page.reason.render_failed`, with the text of the failure in `error`). It keeps whatever words were read, as
`unscored`, and none of its numbers is ever `checked`. A page whose worker failed has `dpi` 0, sizes 0 and no words.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | `int` | The page number, counting from 1. |
| `width_px` | `int` | Width of the page as drawn for the OCR, in pixels. |
| `height_px` | `int` | Height of the page as drawn for the OCR, in pixels. |
| `width_pt` | `float` | Width of the page in PDF points (1/72 inch). |
| `height_pt` | `float` | Height of the page in PDF points. |
| `dpi` | `int` | The resolution the page was drawn at: the scan's own resolution limited to 100-300, or 200 when the page has no scan image, and lowered further so that the longer side of the page stays within 3,000 pixels. |
| `words` | `tuple[Word, ...]` | The words of the page, in reading order, as [`Word`](#word) objects. |
| `status` | `str` | `native` (the PDF's own text layer was legible and was used), `ocr` or `unreadable`. |
| `reason` | `str \| None` | For an `unreadable` page, the `page.reason.*` key that says why. `None` otherwise. |
| `error` | `str \| None` | The text of the failure, when something failed while the page was read. `None` otherwise. |
| `mean_conf` | `float \| None` | The mean confidence of the words, from 0 to 1, or `None` on `native` pages. |
| `unaligned_words` | `int` | How many words have no `char_conf` because their characters could not be matched to their line's. For these words `conf` is the confidence of the line. |
| `rereads` | `Mapping[int, tuple[str, ...]]` | For each line that was read again by the second reading, the readers that ran on it. A line that is absent was not read again. Engine detail, not saved. |
| `reread_report` | `Mapping[str, int]` | Counts of what the second reading did on the page. Engine detail, not saved. |

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json")
page = doc.pages[0]
print(page.number, page.status, page.dpi, page.width_px, page.height_px)
print([round(value, 1) for value in page.box_to_points(page.words[0].box)])
```

```text
# output
1 ocr 200 1654 2339
[52.9, 42.1, 153.0, 61.9]
```

**See also**: [`Document.pages`](document.md#documentpages), [`Document.unreadable_pages`](document.md#documentunreadable_pages), [`Word`](#word).

### `Page.box_to_points`

```text
Page.box_to_points(box: Box) -> Box
```

Convert a box from pixels to PDF points.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `box` | `Box` | required | `(left, top, right, bottom)` in pixels of this page, such as [`Word.box`](#word). |

**Returns**

The same box in points (1/72 inch), scaled by `width_pt / width_px` and `height_pt / height_px`. The JSON stores both forms as `box_px` and `box_pt`.

**Raises**

- `ZeroDivisionError`: The page has `width_px` 0 (a page whose rendering failed).

## `Reason`

Why a word is doubtful, or why a page could not be read: an i18n key and the numbers its text needs.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `str` | The key, from one of three families. `guard.reason.*` explains a doubtful word: `not_in_dictionary`, `close_to` (params `word`), `low_char_conf` (params `char`, `conf`), `mixed_letters_digits`, `odd_chars`, `bad_number_format`, `neighbours_unusual`, `unusual_height`, `unusual_width` and `low_page_quality`. `guard.fix.*` explains a proposed fix: `accent_restored`, `case_restored`, `dictionary_nearest` (params `word`), `engine_alternative` (params `char`, `conf`), `page_vocabulary` (params `count`), `punctuation_restored`, `readers_agree` (params `n`, `of`), `speck_dropped`, `word_split` and `words_joined`. `page.reason.*` explains an unreadable page: `few_words`, `low_confidence` and `render_failed`. |
| `params` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | The values the text needs, such as `{"char": "l", "conf": 0.98}`. Empty when the key needs none. |

**See also**: [`Word`](#word), [`Fix`](#fix), [`Page`](#page-pagereading).

## `Fix`

One proposal of the guard for a word: what to change, how sure it is, and which correction modes apply it.

A proposal exists whether or not it is applied. `modes` says which modes of [`Options.correct`](options.md#options) apply it; an empty
tuple means the proposal is only shown, as a suggestion. The proposal stays on the word after [`Document.undo`](document.md#documentundo).

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `op` | `str` | What the fix does: `text` (replace the text of one word), `join` (join the words in `ids` into one), `segment` (split one word into several) or `drop` (remove a speck that is not a word). |
| `kind` | `str` | The family of the edit: `accent`, `case`, `accent_case`, `letters`, `punct`, `structure` or `number`. |
| `text` | `str` | The new text. |
| `ids` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The ids of the words the fix spans. |
| `source` | `str` | Where the candidate text came from: `dictionary`, `fold`, `punct`, `page`, `ctc_alt`, `masked`, `reading`, `joined`, `join_edit`, `segment` or `drop`; a digit fix has `rule:` followed by the key of the rule that verified it. It is the first of `sources`. |
| `sources` | `tuple[str, ...]` | Every source that proposed the same text. |
| `p_fix` | `float` | The calibrated probability that the new text is the truth. It can be very small: it is a probability, not a score of how good the text looks. |
| `p_keep` | `float` | The calibrated probability that the word as it was read is right. |
| `rule` | `str \| None` | The key of the verifying rule of a digit fix, or `None`. |
| `modes` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The modes that apply the fix: a subset of `("safe", "more")`. |
| `reasons` | `tuple[Reason, ...]` | Up to three `guard.fix.*` reasons. |

**See also**: [`Document.fix_info`](document.md#documentfix_info), [`Document.set_mode`](document.md#documentset_mode), [`Reason`](#reason), [`Word`](#word).

## `Reading`

What one reader of the second reading made of a word of a line it read again.

Engine detail: it is kept on [`Word.readings`](#word) while the document is in memory and is never saved in the JSON.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `str` | The name of the reader that made this reading. |
| `text` | `str \| None` | What the reader read for the word, or `None` when its line could not be aligned with the first reading. |
| `conf` | `float \| None` | The reader's confidence in the word, from 0 to 1, or `None`. |
| `char_conf` | `tuple[float, ...] \| None` | One confidence per character, or `None`. |
| `group` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The ids of the words of the first reading that the reader saw as one: the evidence for a join. A reader that cut the word in two has a space in `text`. |
| `rank` | `int \| None` | The rank of the unit (a line or a zone) the word was read in, 0 being the most doubtful of its page, or `None`. |
| `context` | `bool` | True when the word is in the unit only as context: a neighbour, or a word of a line that did not pass the selection rule. |

**See also**: [`Word`](#word), [`Options`](options.md#options).

## `Number` (`NumberResult`)

`extract.Number` is the class `NumberResult`; `repr` and tracebacks show the long name.

A number of the document and what the rules say about it.

A number on an unreadable page is never `checked`, and [`Document.accept`](document.md#documentaccept) never changes the status: only the
rules do. `unverified` is not an error: a CIF, a French IBAN or an amount written with a space as thousands
separator cannot be confirmed.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `word_ids` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The ids of the words the number is made of: one, or the two to five words of an IBAN written in groups. |
| `text` | `str` | The number as written, such as `"1.893,85"`; the words of a grouped IBAN are joined with a space. |
| `value` | `Decimal \| None` | The exact value as a `Decimal` for `amount`, `percent`, `integer` and `quantity`; `None` for `dni`, `nie`, `cif`, `iban`, `date` and `other`, and for an amount that does not parse. |
| `kind` | `str` | What kind of number it is: `dni`, `nie`, `cif`, `iban`, `percent`, `date`, `integer`, `amount`, `quantity` or `other`. |
| `status` | `str` | `checked` (a verifying rule passes and none fails), `mismatch` (a rule fails: some digit is wrong, not necessarily the one suggested) or `unverified` (nothing confirms it and nothing contradicts it). |
| `rules` | `tuple[RuleResult, ...]` | The [`Rule`](#rule-ruleresult) of every rule that applies to the number. |
| `suggestion` | `DigitSuggestion \| None` | A [`DigitSuggestion`](#digitsuggestion), or `None` when there is none. |

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json")
total = next(number for number in doc.numbers if number.text == "101.913,81")
print(total.kind, total.value, total.status, total.word_ids)
for rule in total.rules:
    print(rule.key, rule.result, rule.verifying)
fix = total.suggestion
print(fix.position, fix.old, fix.new, fix.verified)
```

```text
# output
amount 101913.81 mismatch ('p1w75',)
checks.rule.number_format pass False
checks.rule.total fail True
8 8 5 True
```

**See also**: [`Document.numbers`](document.md#documentnumbers), [`Rule`](#rule-ruleresult), [`DigitSuggestion`](#digitsuggestion), [`Document.use_suggestion`](document.md#documentuse_suggestion).

## `Rule` (`RuleResult`)

`extract.Rule` is the class `RuleResult`; `repr` and tracebacks show the long name.

One rule that involves a number, and whether the number passed it.

A rule is `verifying` when it would fail for any wrong character in the number. Only a verifying rule that passes
can make a number `checked`; the plausibility rules can only fail.

The keys, all in the family `checks.rule.*`: `dni_letter`, `nie_letter` (verifying), `cif_control`, `iban_length`,
`number_format`, `date_valid` and `vat_rate_plausible` (not verifying), `iban_mod97` (verifying only for countries
whose layout has no letter-or-digit position), and the arithmetic rules `line_amount`, `lines_sum`, `vat_amount`,
`withholding_amount` and `total` (verifying when a change of one in the last printed decimal moves the result by at
least a cent).

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `str` | The rule, such as `"checks.rule.total"`. |
| `params` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | The values the rule used. For `checks.rule.total` they are `expected` and `found`. Decimals are strings. |
| `result` | `str` | `"pass"`, `"fail"` or `"not_applicable"`. |
| `verifying` | `bool` | Whether the rule is a verifying one. |

**See also**: [`Number`](#number-numberresult), [`Document.numbers`](document.md#documentnumbers).

## `DigitSuggestion`

A one-digit change that the rules offer for a number: the character at `position` goes from `old` to `new`.

A tie between two changes gives no suggestion at all, and only a number written in a single word can be applied
with [`Document.use_suggestion`](document.md#documentuse_suggestion).

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `position` | `int` | The index in [`Number.text`](#number-numberresult) of the character to change, counting from 0. |
| `old` | `str` | The character that is there now. |
| `new` | `str` | The character to put there. |
| `verified` | `bool` | True only when a verifying rule fails with the number as read and passes with this one change and with no other, and no plausibility rule objects. |
| `rule` | `str` | The key of the verifying rule when `verified` is true, or of the failing rule the change would satisfy when it is not. |

**See also**: [`Number`](#number-numberresult), [`Document.use_suggestion`](document.md#documentuse_suggestion).

## `Invoice` (`InvoiceFields`)

`extract.Invoice` is the class `InvoiceFields`; `repr` and tracebacks show the long name.

The fields of an invoice. A field that was not found is `None`, never a guess.

Only page 1 is read for fields, so a multi-page invoice is not covered. A layout that Extract has not seen can
leave a field empty. Each field is a [`Cell`](#cell); its trust is `Document.field_status(cell)`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | `Cell \| None` | The invoice number. |
| `date` | `Cell \| None` | The date of the invoice. |
| `subtotal` | `Cell \| None` | The amount before taxes, labelled `base imponible`, `subtotal` or similar. |
| `vat` | `tuple[VatPair, ...]` | The VAT lines, as [`VatPair`](#vatpair) objects. Empty when none was found. |
| `withholding` | `Cell \| None` | The withholding amount. It is never `checked`, because a document may print it with or without a minus sign. |
| `total` | `Cell \| None` | The total. |
| `currency` | `str \| None` | `"EUR"`, `"USD"` or `"GBP"`, from a symbol or a code on the page, or `None`. A plain string, not a `Cell`. |
| `lines` | `tuple[InvoiceLine, ...]` | The lines of the invoice, as [`InvoiceLine`](#invoiceline) objects. Empty when no table was found. |
| `withholding_rate` | `Cell \| None` | The `Cell` of the withholding rate, as printed. |

**Example**

```python
import extract

doc = extract.load("invoice.extract.json")
invoice = doc.invoice
print(invoice.number.text, invoice.date.text, invoice.currency, len(invoice.lines), len(invoice.vat))
total = invoice.total
print(total.text, total.word_ids, total.page, doc.field_status(total), invoice.withholding)
```

```text
# output
F-2026-0498 20/01/2025 EUR 4 1
101.913,81 ('p1w75',) 1 mismatch None
```

**See also**: [`Document.invoice`](document.md#documentinvoice), [`Cell`](#cell), [`VatPair`](#vatpair), [`InvoiceLine`](#invoiceline), [`Document.field_status`](document.md#documentfield_status).

## `InvoiceLine`

One line of an invoice. A column that was not found is `None`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `description` | `Cell \| None` | The description of the line. |
| `quantity` | `Cell \| None` | The quantity. |
| `unit_price` | `Cell \| None` | The price of one unit. |
| `amount` | `Cell \| None` | The amount of the line, which the rule `checks.rule.line_amount` compares with quantity times price. |

**See also**: [`Invoice`](#invoice-invoicefields), [`Cell`](#cell).

## `VatPair`

A VAT rate with its base and amount, each a [`Cell`](#cell) or `None`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | `Cell \| None` | The `Cell` of the rate, as printed. |
| `amount` | `Cell \| None` | The VAT amount. |
| `base` | `Cell \| None` | The taxable base next to the rate, when the invoice prints one. `None` otherwise. |

**See also**: [`Invoice`](#invoice-invoicefields), [`Cell`](#cell).

## `Cell`

A field of an invoice: its text and the words it was read from.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `str` | The text of the field as read, such as `"101.913,81"`. Not a number: the number is in [`Document.numbers`](document.md#documentnumbers). |
| `word_ids` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The ids of the words the text was made from. |
| `page` | `int` | The page number the field is on. Fields are read from page 1. |

**See also**: [`Invoice`](#invoice-invoicefields), [`Document.field_status`](document.md#documentfield_status).

## Helper functions of `extract.types`

These three are not exported by `extract`; import them from `extract.types` when you need to build or take apart word ids.

### `word_id`

```text
word_id(page: int, index: int) -> str
```

Build the id of a word from its page and its position.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `int` | required | The page number, counting from 1. |
| `index` | `int` | required | The position of the word on the page in reading order, counting from 0. |

**Returns**

The id, `p{page}w{index}`: `word_id(3, 17)` is `"p3w17"`.

**Example**

```python
from extract import types

print(types.word_id(3, 17), types.base_id("p3w17#1"), types.page_of("p3w17"))
```

```text
# output
p3w17 p3w17 3
```

**See also**: [`base_id`](#base_id), [`page_of`](#page_of), [`Word`](#word).

### `base_id`

```text
base_id(token: str) -> str
```

Return the id of the word a token comes from.

A word that the guard segmented is split into tokens whose ids have the form `p3w17#1`; `p3w17` is their base. An
id without `#` is its own base.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | `str` | required | A word id or a token id. |

**Returns**

The word id, without the `#` part.

**See also**: [`word_id`](#word_id), [`Document.tokens`](document.md#documenttokens), [`Document.word`](document.md#documentword).

### `page_of`

```text
page_of(word: str) -> int
```

Return the page number that a word id belongs to.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word` | `str` | required | A word id such as `"p3w17"`, or a token id such as `"p3w17#1"`. |

**Returns**

The page number, counting from 1.

**Raises**

- `ValueError`: `word` is not a word id.

**See also**: [`word_id`](#word_id), [`base_id`](#base_id).

# docs/reference/events.md

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the docstrings. Edit the docstrings, not this file. -->

# Events

The events of a read: progress, notices and the end of the job.

Pass a function as `on_event` to [`read`](functions.md#read), [`Reader.read`](reader.md#readerread) or [`Document.export`](document.md#documentexport) and it is called with one event after
another, in the thread that called, while the job runs. All of them are frozen dataclasses and subclasses of [`Event`](#event);
all are importable from `extract` ([`extract.PageRead`](#pageread), [`extract.Warning`](#warning), ...). A screen gets them as JSON through
`to_dict`, with i18n keys and parameters only.

The events of one `Reader.read` come in this order:

1. [`Started`](#started), once, with the page count.
2. For every page, a `PageRead` and then a [`Progress`](#progress). Pages arrive in the order the workers finish them, which is not
   always 1, 2, 3: digital and cached pages come first.
3. `Warning`, at any moment between the first and the last event, as many as there are notices.
4. [`DocumentRead`](#documentread), once, with the summary of the document.
5. [`Finished`](#finished), last: `"done"`, `"stopped"` after a cancel, or `"failed"` after an exception. The exception is raised
   after the event.

A read that fails before the PDF is open (a missing file, [`UnsupportedFile`](errors.md#unsupportedfile), [`PasswordProtected`](errors.md#passwordprotected)) sends
